# QA API Testing

## Derive the real contract

Inspect global server configuration, route/controller, guards/middleware, request schema/DTO, service/state machine, persistence schema, background jobs/events, client types, and existing tests. Resolve method, path, content type, auth mechanism, input transformations, statuses, success/error shapes, state mutation, uniqueness/ownership, and side effects. Flag specification conflicts.

## Prove prerequisites

Confirm exact target/base URL and health/readiness separately. Record database, cache, queue, object store, mail/payment/AI, and fallback modes that affect the result. Use isolated accounts and redact secrets. A readiness failure blocks dependent cases; it is not evidence that the endpoint implementation is defective.

## Select the relevant matrix

| Area | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Transport | method, path, headers/content type, status, response/error shape |
| Input | valid, missing, empty, null, wrong type, malformed, min/max, duplicate, unknown field |
| Identity | anonymous, valid session/token, expiry/refresh/logout, wrong role |
| Authorization | owner, unrelated user, nonexistent resource, already-transitioned resource |
| State | persisted result, related records, timestamps, idempotency, duplicate prevention |
| Resilience | dependency unavailable, retry, timeout, rate limit, repeated/concurrent request |

Do not mechanically execute irrelevant rows. Use a session-aware client for cookie flows and never print cookie/token values.

## Verify asynchronous behavior in phases

1. Assert immediate HTTP acknowledgement and duplicate handling.
2. Observe the relevant event/socket/job state when available.
3. Read authoritative API/database state with a bounded timeout.
4. Verify timeout/failure and retry/idempotency separately.
5. Record whether real queue/cache/event infrastructure or a fallback was active.

An accepted `2xx` is not a pass when persistence or eventual side effects are part of the contract.

## Concurrency and abuse safety

Use small controlled request counts only in local or explicitly authorized test environments. Never load-test production without authorization specifying target, rate, duration, monitoring, stop conditions, and cleanup.

## Automation and evidence

Use unit tests for pure service behavior, controller tests for delegation/mapping, full transport integration for real validation/guards/auth, and sanitized scripts for live smoke. For every case record ID, sanitized request, expected and actual status/body/state, duration if relevant, infrastructure mode, and exact test/command. Use `qa-automation` for persistent coverage.

## Project execution context

### Facts

- Frontend is Next.js 16/React 19 with TanStack Query; backend is NestJS 11 under /api except health endpoints.
- Prisma/PostgreSQL is authoritative; Redis may fall back in development.
- Global DTO validation whitelists fields and rejects undeclared fields.
- Authentication uses httpOnly access_token and refresh_token cookies.
- AI matches and suggestions are queued; Socket.IO drives realtime client invalidation.

### Commands

- pnpm qa:validate — QA adapter, manifest, hook, MCP, and platform-parity validation
- pnpm check — full repository gate
- pnpm --dir backend test -- <pattern> --runInBand — focused backend
- pnpm --dir frontend exec vitest run <file> — focused frontend

### Priority risks

- Authentication, refresh/logout, ownership, roles, and cross-user isolation
- Request/friend/session state transitions, duplicate actions, and timezone overlap
- Queued AI work, socket delivery, retry/idempotency, reconnect, and eventual consistency
- DTO/client contract drift, stale query cache, accessibility, and responsive layout

### Boundaries

- OpenAI/AI provider, Redis/BullMQ, S3, email, database, Socket.IO, and remote environments
- In-memory fallback is not evidence for multi-instance Redis, queue, or socket behavior
